tasks.title: Document shared configuration conventions and correct the I/O boundary
tasks.spec: ## Repository: config — Files, proposed entry, checks and completion evidence; Required behavior: The common entry; Acceptance evidence 1-3, 5-6; Non-goals, Risks and impact statements. Document reuse of the existing shared config files, bin/pulse-eslint.js, bin/pulse-workflows.js, src/workflow-policy.ts and existing tests without changing those modules. Keep script logic small and pure, with file and process I/O in bin/ entry points. No shared config or target pin changes. Add ## Code conventions directly after ## Code design; extend a section already present on current main instead of adding a duplicate. Re-read current main before editing (inspected clone bc87049); apply the Counterexamples to the entry. Implement the section's Contradiction correction: replace exactly the existing AGENTS.md:51 with - Keep logic pure. I/O (files, child processes, `process.env`, `process.exit`, `console`) stays in the `bin/` entry points. Preserve line 52 about dependency wiring and every other existing line. Acceptance evidence 1 permits exactly this one replacement in config; it does not permit other removals.

acceptance.expected: prints exactly AGENTS.md; no product code, test, CI, dependency, README.md, version or generated-output changes
prints exactly 1 removed line and no other removal. The literal output is: -- Keep logic pure. I/O (HTTP, SQLite, files, `process.env`, `console`) stays in `main.ts` and the server or client modules.

acceptance.command: grep -Fx -- '- Keep logic pure. I/O (files, child processes, `process.env`, `process.exit`, `console`) stays in the `bin/` entry points.' AGENTS.md
acceptance.expected: prints exactly the corrected literal line: - Keep logic pure. I/O (files, child processes, `process.env`, `process.exit`, `console`) stays in the `bin/` entry points.
prints an integer at least 1; the exact canonical meta URL is present
prints exactly 200 for an unauthenticated request

Reading confirms: Add ## Code conventions directly after ## Code design; extend a section already present on current main instead of adding a duplicate. The entry directs agents to search the shared config files, bin/ and existing tests before writing, extract the second copy into a shared helper, and keep functions small and pure with file and process I/O in bin/. Common prose is at most three lines after the heading. It links the convention without copying its seven rules or examples, replaces only the contradicting line 51 with the exact corrected line, preserves line 52 and all other existing text and stricter rules, and adds no enforcement or refactor.
exit 0 using the unchanged package.json:40 check script; report an unrelated baseline failure as a known limit without fixing out-of-scope files
no changed or untracked path except AGENTS.md (or empty output after committing); in particular no dist/, lockfile, test or tooling changes

The PR body names the issue and supplies the AGENTS.md-only diff, the single removed line and exact corrected line from the Contradiction correction, link/heading grep outputs, and the bun run check command and actual result. It records known limits; states documentation-only performance impact none expected and security impact no; and leaves Acceptance evidence 6 as a post-merge feature-close check with the main SHA and repeated link/meaning checks, without claiming it ran before merge.

acceptance.command: verified_main_sha=$(gh api repos/lorenzh/pulse-config/commits/main --jq .sha) && printf '%s\n' "$verified_main_sha" && gh api "repos/lorenzh/pulse-config/contents/AGENTS.md?ref=$verified_main_sha" --jq .content | base64 --decode
acceptance.expected: Deferred until feature close after this target PR merges (not a pre-merge task gate): record the main commit SHA returned by GitHub and read AGENTS.md at that exact SHA. Repeat Acceptance evidence 2-3 on that content: canonical URL present at least once, exactly 1 Code conventions heading, URL HTTP 200, and the three meanings. This implements this target's part of Acceptance evidence 6.
